title: The Local Deadlock
subtitle: Two threads wait forever with zero CPU

brief.narrative: Thread A locks account 1 then waits for account 2. Thread B locks account 2 then waits for account 1. Both block forever.
symptoms: Thread Pool metrics diverge from the service-level symptom
The problem reproduces only under the triggering workload
Logs contain enough evidence to distinguish cause from consequence

rootCause.question: Which root cause explains all of the evidence?

options.text: A socket/file-descriptor leak exhausted the per-process limit.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: CPU oversubscription created scheduling and cache-locality overhead.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Opposite lock ordering created a circular wait.
options.feedback: Correct. Deadlock requires mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait. Break at least one condition by design.
This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

fix.question: Which fix is safest for production?

options.text: Size CPU-bound workers near the effective CPU quota, batch work, and measure run queue, throttling, switches, and throughput.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Define a global lock order, acquire in that order, keep lock scope small, and use timeouts only as a recovery safety net.
options.feedback: Correct. Deadlock requires mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait. Break at least one condition by design.

options.text: Reduce working sets, cap concurrency/cache memory, add RAM only after measurement, and alert on major faults and swap activity.
